comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page and 2026–27 Course Catalogue establish a 180-EC Dutch-language Philosophy bachelor. Year 1 totals 60 EC across practical philosophy, logic and the linguistic turn, theoretical philosophy, history of philosophy, academic writing and research skills. Year 2 totals 60 EC across Text, Context and Debate, non-Western philosophy, two philosophy-of-science modules, the philosophical practicum, specialisation courses and a philosophy elective. Year 3 totals 60 EC: 42 EC of free choice, 6 EC of thesis-oriented specialisation and the 12-EC bachelor thesis. The published regular programme has no formal route requiring selection, so all genuine choice spaces remain aggregate rather than being invented.

core: History of philosophy across ancient, medieval, modern and contemporary traditions
Ethics, value theory, justice, political and social philosophy
Metaphysics, epistemology, perception, language, cognition and reality
Formal logic, argument analysis, critical thinking and the linguistic turn
Philosophy of science, scientific evidence and relations among philosophy, science and technology
Close reading, philosophical writing, research methods and independent thesis work
adjacent: Ethics and politics as a coherent direction in justice, institutions and moral judgment
Mind, language and world as a coherent direction in cognition, perception, knowledge and reality
Comparative and global philosophy across Chinese, Indian, Islamic and intercultural traditions
questions: What justice requires and how moral and political institutions should be assessed
Whether perception and reason give reliable knowledge of reality
What distinguishes scientific knowledge and evidence from other forms of knowledge
How philosophical ideas shape identity, culture and society

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Philosophy, argument and intellectual history
alternatives.concept: Builds the broadest available UCR philosophy pathway from ethics, mind, self, political philosophy, logic and argument, complemented by intellectual history, literature and cultural interpretation. It covers UvA’s cross-subdisciplinary core while remaining less philosophically specialised than the comparator.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines all five available UCR philosophy courses with political philosophy, logic, rhetoric, intellectual history and interpretive humanities; the label names its philosophical and argumentative centre without overstating specialist depth.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
alternatives.concept: Concentrates practical philosophy around ethics, political thought, human rights, law, institutions, social theory, conflict and public argument. It turns the programme’s evidenced moral and political questions into a materially different interdisciplinary UCR curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is dominated by ethics and political philosophy, human rights and public law, institutions, social theory, conflict and argumentative communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ten courses in archaeology, literature, general history and rhetoric with comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and an advanced history research seminar. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than broad philosophical and intellectual history.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Law, Society & Justice is completed in the first semester before Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and eight level-3 courses occur after introductory philosophy, politics, law and sociology.

alternatives.label: Mind, language, cognition and philosophy of science
alternatives.concept: Develops theoretical philosophy through mind, perception, knowledge, language, cognition and science, supported by logic, psycholinguistics, cognitive science, machine learning and AI ethics. It studies representation and agency across philosophical, psychological and computational perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum clusters philosophy of mind, emotion and self with psycholinguistics, cognition, brain and behaviour, logic, meaning, machine learning, AI ethics and empirical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in political philosophy, law, history, archaeology, literature and international politics with brain and behaviour, neurobiology, perception and action, psycholinguistics, social and experimental psychology, higher cognition, programming, machine learning, AI ethics and an advanced psychology research seminar. Compared with the ethics route, it replaces law, institutions and social theory with sustained study of mind, language and science.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Introduction to Brain & Behavior is completed in semester 1 before Perception & Action, Psycholinguistics, Higher Order Functions and Advanced Research Seminar; introductory philosophy, rhetoric and brain science precede advanced mind, language and research work. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and seven level-3 courses occur in Years 2 and 3.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the broad history, practical and theoretical philosophy, logic and argument core. Ethics/politics/justice and mind/language/knowledge/science each produce a coherent, feasible and pairwise distinct additional curriculum. Comparative and global philosophy is valuable evidence within the broad closest match but cannot form a fourth alternative under the three-programme maximum.

notes.text: UvA provides a continuous 180-EC Philosophy curriculum with dedicated sequences in practical philosophy, theoretical philosophy, logic, history of philosophy, philosophy of science, research methods and a required thesis. UCR offers five dedicated Philosophy courses and builds the three alternatives with Politics, Law, Communication, History, Literature, Sociology, Cognitive Science, Psychology and AI. These are defensible interdisciplinary pathways but do not reproduce UvA’s specialist disciplinary depth or required Philosophy thesis.
